thread:
autoscaler-bot: :warning: Pager: private-cluster 'acme-nyc' GPU pool at 98% queue depth, provisioning failures >= 5m. Escalation to infra oncall.
Ava (infra-oncall): paging in, looking. what's the customer impact?
Jamal (cust-success): customer reports high latency for inference jobs, some requests 503ing. They've opened a support ticket.
Diego (sre-lead): seeing large inflight queue on the scheduler: `pending_pods=312`, `backlog_rate=~200/min`. Autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts that fail with "node bootstrap timeout".
Priya (eng-runtime): any recent config change to the private provisioner image or AMI?
Ava (infra-oncall): not from us. This cluster uses customer-provided AMI overlay. logs show `imagepull backoff` on k8s node bootstrap hook.
autoscaler-bot: scale_attempt id=8423 -> requested 8 nodes, success=false, failure_reason="bootstrap timeout"
Ava (infra-oncall): pulling node-provisioner logs:
```
2026-03-15T03:14:02Z provisioner: starting boot sequence
2026-03-15T03:15:20Z cloud-init: failed to fetch userdata: 404
2026-03-15T03:16:50Z kubelet: crashloop backoff, error="failed to start: missing certs"
```
Priya (eng-runtime): missing certs... customer uses custom KMS config for HSM. Could be because our init container can't reach their KMS endpoint during bootstrap.
Diego (sre-lead): that fits with imagepulls failing (init container pulls secrets). But why now? network path looks green earlier.
Jamal (cust-success): customer says they rotated a key last night and rolled a new image. Might be correlation.
Ava (infra-oncall): immediate mitigation idea: cordon new nodes from joining to prevent flapping, then scale a separate pool without the custom AMI to drain some queue. Can we spin a fallback pool?
Priya (eng-runtime): We can create a short-lived fallback pool (pool-fallback-gpu) using our verified public AMI that doesn't depend on their KMS. But need approval from SRE to route traffic and we must avoid violating tenancy/isolation requirements.
Diego (sre-lead): approved for temporary capacity to reduce customer impact. Create pool and allow the autoscaler to target it as fallback. Also increase max_nodes on cluster autoscaler to allow more nodes.
Ava (infra-oncall): creating pool now: `rctl pool create --name pool-fallback-gpu --size 0 --max 20 --ami=redwood-gpu-verified-v2`
deploy-bot: pool creation accepted, id=pf-9921, awaiting warmup.
Ava (infra-oncall): bumping autoscaler max from 30 to 60 for this cluster: `kubectl patch configmap autoscaler-config -p '{"data":{"max_nodes":"60"}}'`
autoscaler-bot: config update acknowledged, new max_nodes=60
Priya (eng-runtime): submitting a temporary routing rule: runbooks/route-fallback -> prefer pool-fallback-gpu for tenant=acme-nyc.
Diego (sre-lead): while that's happening, can we surface an escalation to customer success that some jobs will run on fallback instances (different AMI), might need data locality note? Jamal?
Jamal (cust-success): told customer about fallback, they accepted as short term. they're worried about ephemeral token access for some workloads.
Ava (infra-oncall): warmup logs: `node pf-9921-01 ready`, `nv_driver init ok`, `kubelet registered`. Starting to schedule pending pods.
Priya (eng-runtime): good, but some pods still pending due to `nodeSelector: custom-ami=true`. We need a quick patch to remove the selector for affected deployments so they can land on fallback nodes.
Diego (sre-lead): I'm going to run a temporary admission override: patch the namespace `acme-nyc-inference` to drop the nodeSelector via `kubectl -n acme-nyc-inference patch deploy --all --type json -p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/template/spec/nodeSelector/custom-ami"}]'` — testing on one deployment first.
Ava (infra-oncall): patch applied to `inference-worker-1`. Pod rescheduled -> `container creating` -> `started`. Latency dropping. queue depth down to 80.
autoscaler-bot: scale_event: pool-fallback-gpu scaled to 6 nodes, allocated 120 gpus.
Jamal (cust-success): customer confirming some jobs now running, reports success for a subset. They're still seeing intermittent 503s for non-fallback regions.
Priya (eng-runtime): while we mitigate, need to capture root cause: likely customer AMI rotation + KMS endpoint change causing bootstrap failures. We'll coordinate with them to roll forward certs.
Diego (sre-lead): action items: 1) Keep pool-fallback up for 2 hours and monitor. 2) Work with customer to fix KMS/AMI so we can revert routing. 3) Revert autoscaler max to previous after drain. 4) Postmortem if root cause confirmed. I'll take incident lead.
Ava (infra-oncall): oncall handoff in 2h -> tagging next oncall. Adding temporary alert throttles to avoid noisy pages while we stabilize: `alert-mute --scope=acme-nyc --window=2h`
Jamal (cust-success): updating customer ticket with status, mitigation steps, ETA ~2h.
Priya (eng-runtime): collecting bootstrap logs and packaging for the customer: `tar -czf acme-nyc-bootstrap-logs.tgz /var/log/provisioner/*`
Diego (sre-lead): recorded for postmortem. Great work. I'll keep this thread as the incident record. Marking severity P1 -> downgraded to P2 as customer impact reduced but ongoing work.
Ava (infra-oncall): leaving notes for next oncall: fallback pool pf-9921 must be drained before reverting nodeSelector changes, do not delete pf-9921 until all tenant jobs confirmed on primary pool.
autoscaler-bot: incident closed flag toggled=false (ongoing).
deploy-bot: ran cleanup check, no failed jobs on fallback pool.
Jamal (cust-success): customer thanks the team, will coordinate key rotation fix on their side.
Diego (sre-lead): thanks all — will post follow-up remediation and timeline.
Ava (infra-oncall): handing off to @next-oncall in 2m.
next-oncall (automated note): acknowledged handoff.
